title: The First 15 Minutes of a Workshop with a Senior Team (and the 5 Mistakes that lose them)
author: Workshop Bank
summary: Opening with a facilitator losing a C-suite room the moment he hands out Lego bricks, the piece argues senior leaders decide within the first 15 minutes whether a session is worth their attention, because their bandwidth is more constrained and more protected than most people's. It walks through five specific mistakes that lose senior rooms: opening with credentials instead of the deliverable, using a familiar framework instead of their own data, running an activity that feels beneath them, talking too long before letting them work, and failing to translate the session into the business-impact language they're measured on. Each mistake is paired with a concrete fix, such as replacing a CV-style opening with a one-sentence outcome statement, or reframing a soft label like 'team effectiveness' into the specific metric a VP loses sleep over.
points: Senior leaders decide within the first 15 minutes whether a session deserves their full attention, because their bandwidth is more constrained and fiercely protected.
Skip the credentials-first opening; senior rooms respond to a one-sentence outcome statement ('By 3pm this team will have agreed three priorities...') instead of a CV.
Avoid familiar leadership frameworks and generic team-building activities (the 'Lego moment') with senior groups — use their own real, stuck decisions instead.
Get senior participants working within five minutes; every extra minute of setup spends their scarce attention on your voice instead of their thinking.
Translate soft sounding labels ('team effectiveness') into the specific metric a VP is measured on and losing sleep over, since framing — not content — is often what loses the room.
quotes: A senior leader operates closer to the limit of their decision capacity than almost anyone.
Anything that eats attention without improving the decision in front of them gets filed as waste.
The one credential that lands with this group is the deliverable. Open with the outcome instead of your CV.
Senior leaders will do serious work gladly. They’ll debate a hard question for an hour.
The facilitators who impress senior groups most are almost always the ones who say the least.
Nobody objects to “team effectiveness.” They just privately downgrade the session from “worth my focus” to “worth showing up to”.
